note: Each entry is an item.record payload as tools/tillr-item's itemPayload defines it (apply.go, schema.go): item_id, title, body_ref, state, criteria, blocked_by, design_doc, allowed_paths. No field outside that payload is written here, and no criterion is copied from the archive verbatim unless it is still true of today's tree. Criteria are the final words: tools/tillr-item freezes a criterion's text once its state is non-empty (carryCriteria, rule criterion-frozen), so a rewrite after the seed is refused. allowed_paths is the fence staging renders and the loop enforces: an item without one is refused at staging, and three such refusals halt the loop.

items.title: Landed work leaves the queue for an archive view, and the queue says where it went

criteria.text: An item in `landed`, `resolved_elsewhere` or `closed` is not drawn on the rail; the rail's row set is the queue and nothing else.
An archive view lists them in the same order with the same row shape, reachable from the header's landed count, and the filter reaches both views.
A summary band shows the last few items that reached a terminal state, with the count of finished items always visible on the header.

The queue lists only live items: a landed or closed item is reachable from the archive view and from search, appears in the queue for no longer than the tick that landed it, and the board states in one line where landed work went — so a reader never mistakes an empty queue for an empty store.

items.title: Items with no rank are drawn as their own block, so id order is never read as priority

criteria.text: The items the seed stores with no rank — every blocked, landed and closed row, 16 of 65 today — are drawn under one heading that says no priority is recorded, instead of continuing the ranked list in id order: measured today `item-seed-01` (blocked) sorts after rank `z` and nothing on the screen distinguishes that from a recorded priority.
The heading names how many items are unranked and how to rank them, so the state is correctable from the board rather than only from the seed file.
The order stays one rule: the server, the client (`queueOrder`) and the drain planner agree on ranked-then-unranked, asserted by a case that reads a store holding both kinds.

A payload that carries no `rank` on ANY item is drawn as a server that predates the field, not as 55 unranked items: measured 2026-11-14, a `tillr-view` built before the rank field made every row unranked, and the client's rank-then-id order therefore rendered the whole board in id order with nothing on screen saying why. The client says which build served the page and refuses to fall back to id order silently; a server whose build cannot be named is drawn as unverified rather than as authoritative.

items.title: Every question waiting on the owner is discoverable from the board in one place, with a link into Vantage

criteria.text: One place on the board lists every item whose design document carries an unanswered question — the item, its question ids, and for each question a link built as `<vantage base>/#/<path>#<OQ-id>` — reachable without knowing which item to click first.

The list, the rail state and the header count agree with the planner: an item in the list is held, not dispatched, and an item whose last question is answered leaves the list on the next read rather than after a restart.
With no Vantage base URL configured the links are still drawn, are correct, and go nowhere, and the view says so in one line — the board never probes that URL.

items.title: The composed-pipeline case judges a candidate through the real exported registry, not a one-check stub

criteria.text: `tools/tillr-drain/pipeline_test.go` plans from `python3 tools/fork-check.py --registry-json` and gates through `--gate python3 tools/fork-check.py --since <base> --no-wait`, so the case that proves the pipeline exercises the in-process checks and the real declaration set: today `rg -n 'fork-check' tools/tillr-drain -g '*_test.go'` returns nothing, and the case at `pipeline_test.go:223` runs `/bin/true` against a registry the fixture writes with one trivial check.

The run leg names a backend whose adapter is the echo provider, so the record the pipeline writes carries a `backend` a reader can check, and the case changes no production file — the passing number is zero non-test files in the commit.

items.title: The planner never dispatches two items whose fences overlap, so one tick cannot put two writers on one directory

criteria.text: A tick offering two lanes to three ready items that all fence `tools/tillr-view/` dispatches ONE of them, and the decision for the other two names the item it was deferred behind: measured 2026-11-14, the top three in-queue items fence exactly that one directory and `drain plan` dispatching two of them was read as safe because they land in separate worktrees. Two worktrees editing one file is one writer too many, arrived at a step later.

The fence text the planner compares is the one staging writes to the lane (`.tillr/lanes/<lane>/fence`), read through the same parser the escape check uses, so a plan and the check that convicts a run cannot disagree about where a lane may write.

An item with no fence, or a fence naming the repository root, is not deferred: it is refused as an item that would fence nothing, because the alternative is a rule that silently serialises the whole queue behind one blanket.

items.title: Each lane gets its own durable directory, so two lanes cannot clobber each other's scratch even when their fences are disjoint

criteria.text: `run.Exec` stops handing a worker the coordinator's `YOLO_DURABLE_DIR`: it removes every inherited `YOLO_DURABLE_DIR=` from `os.Environ()` and exports `<laneDir>/durable/<run_id>` instead, a path outside `<laneDir>/worktree` so the fence never has to admit it. Measured 2026-11-14: `tools/tillr-run/run/exec.go:140` is `cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TILLR_RUN_ID="+req.RunID, "TILLR_LANE_ID="+laneID)`, so the whole environment passes through and every lane — and every `just tillr-build` a lane runs — writes `/workspace/.yolo/durable`. `--lanes 2` is unsafe until this lands even with disjoint git fences, because the fences describe tracked paths and this directory is gitignored.

Two lanes running at once write disjoint durable directories, and a test drives it: two runs are launched concurrently and each child's `YOLO_DURABLE_DIR` is its own per-run path — neither equal to the coordinator's, neither equal to the other's, and each inside that lane's own tree. The negative control is today's behaviour, where both children report the coordinator's path; the case must fail against it.

The brief's fence section carries a bullet naming the per-run durable path, because `stage.go`'s `OutOfFence` constant (`tools/tillr-drain/drain/stage.go:158`, threaded to the template as `OUT_OF_FENCE_PATHS` at `:722`) is the only place a worker is told where its scratch belongs. A scratch directory a worker cannot find is a scratch directory it puts in the repository, which is the fence violation this item exists to prevent.

items.title: The seed owns an item's definition, its intake state and its rank — the store owns everything the store learns

criteria.text: `sameDefinition` (`tools/tillr-item/item/seed.go`) ignores `items.state` and `criteria[].state`: the seed file supplies an item's definition, its intake state at first insert, and its rank, and a seed whose only difference from the store is runtime state applies instead of refusing with `seed-conflict`. Measured 2026-11-14: the next seed after `item-obs-filter` landed was refused on `criterion c1 state is "done" in the store and "" in the seed`, and the operator had to apologise to the file by hand.

`plan.rerank` preserves the stored runtime state: a rank change re-ranks a row without resetting a `landed` or `in-progress` item to `in-queue`. `tools/tillr-item/item/apply.go`'s `ON CONFLICT(item_id) DO UPDATE` sets `state = excluded.state` today, so deleting the two comparisons in c1 alone would turn every re-rank into a resurrection — the fix is the pair, and the criterion names both because either alone is a worse bug than the conflict.

A test pins the pair: a store holding a `landed` item with `done` criteria is re-seeded from a file that states the item `in-queue` with empty criterion states and a new rank, and the store's state, every criterion's state and the new rank all survive. The negative control is the same seed against the unfixed code, which must fail on `seed-conflict`.

The mechanism is the store's, not a write-back: nothing in the drain, the loop or the verdict step writes `config/tillr/seed-items.json`. Mechanism (a) was refused because an uncommitted write dirties the main checkout and trips the host boundary, while a commit moves the trunk outside `tillr land pass` and invalidates `gated_tree == landed_tree`.

items.title: The output-cap recovery never fires on a virtual model row, because `_modelForMessage` compares a selection id against a wire id

criteria.text: `_modelForMessage` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:919`) resolves the message's model by comparing `model.id` against `message.model`, which fails for every virtual row: a message records the WIRE id while a virtual selection's `id` is the row's own. The fix compares `message.model` against `model.wireId ?? model.id` -- the same wire-id rule `getBranchSelection` already uses -- so `sameModel` is true again. Measured 2026-11-14 from the message itself: `provider: "openrouter"`, `model: "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017:floor"` (the wire id of the `@300k` twin), while the selected row's id is `...floor@300k`. A test drives a virtual selection and a message carrying the wire id and asserts `sameModel` is true; the negative control is today's comparison, which reports false.

With `sameModel` true, `compaction.outputCapRecovery` fires for the measured shape: a `length` stop whose `usage.output` equals the row's `maxTokens` (32768) and whose content is one thinking block with no text and no `toolCall`. `isRecoverableLength(message, messageModel.maxTokens, {atCapIsRecoverable: true})` returns true for that shape -- it already does, and the default `models: ["deepseek"]` already matches -- so the item proves the whole route end to end rather than only the comparison: one bounded compaction-and-retry, not a second one. This is the criterion the predecessor could not reach, and it was resolved by reading the code, not by guessing.

The recovery is delivered as a patch in the fork series under `yolo-packs/pi-fork/`, not as a local edit to a checkout: `bin/pi-forks check --lane <lane> --fork pi` passes, `yolo pack lint yolo-packs/pi-fork` passes, and the exported series is committed here. A commit left only in `.forks/` deploys nothing.

items.title: A turn that stopped on `length` settles as `finished`, because the stop-watch has no `length` branch

criteria.text: `yolo-packs/matt/files/extensions/working-stopwatch.ts` handles `error`, `aborted`, `stop` and `toolUse` in its `message_end` handler but has no `length` branch, so a truncation falls through to the default and settles the run with `outcome: "finished"`. It gains a branch that refuses `finished` when the message stopped on `length` and carried neither non-blank text nor a tool call. Measured 2026-11-14T17:04:07Z: the assistant message stopped `length` with one 108,422-character thinking block, and 77 ms later `foreground-run-v1` recorded `outcome: "finished"` for a turn that produced nothing.

A test drives a `length` stop with no text and no tool call through the stop-watch and asserts the settled outcome is not `finished`; the negative control is the same message with one text block, which must still settle `finished`. The case name appears in the suite's own output, because a green suite that never printed it proves only that the file parses.

The 32k cap's comment in `tag-personal/config/yolo-jail/config.d/personal.toml` stops promising a replacement nobody scheduled: it says what the cap is FOR now, names the recovery that breaks the loop, and drops the "until loop detection lands" clause, which has been false since `outputCapRecovery` shipped. A comment that describes a future that did not arrive is how the next reader concludes the cap is temporary and removes it.

`docs/pi/connection-error-turn-death-2026-10-18.md` gains the output-cap branch of its own question, or a sibling is written beside it and cross-linked: what a `length` stop is, why a reasoning loop reaches it, what pi retries (compaction, once), and what the settlement record says. Today the document's subject is connection errors and it never mentions the cap, `32768`, `length` or `outputCapRecovery` -- which made the predecessor's `body_ref` point at a document that could not answer its own item.

items.title: A drain that has refused every candidate it ever produced reads like a drain that is merely unlucky

criteria.text: The blast radius is measured and reported: a refusal that rejects every candidate is not a per-item failure, so the loop names it as such rather than counting it as one tick's `Rejected`. Measured cost of the window: three ticks, 33.3M tokens, $0.185, two items left `in-progress` by `failCandidate` for a `Gate` that never ran. Whether this becomes a stop condition or a `repeated-refusal` report is the implementer's call, but a drain that has refused every candidate it produced since it started must not look like a drain that is merely unlucky.

items.title: A plan holds an item whose design document carries an open question, and one whose document is gone

criteria.text: The planner emits `question-open` for an item whose `design_doc` carries an unanswered question and `design-doc-missing` for one that names a document not in the tree, and it learns both from **Vantage's own index** — `vantage-check index --format json`, whose `questions[]` carries `id`, `state`, `preference`, `title`, `leaning`, `blockedOn` and `line` per document — rather than from a second parser in this repository. The order of the three answers is fixed: the tool's answer wins; the tool absent or erroring is `questions-unknown`, never `no questions`; a document naming no file stays `design-doc-missing`.

A test drives all three through `Plan` against a fixture repository and a stubbed index: an item whose document carries an unanswered question holds with reason `question-open` and the question's id in the decision; the same item dispatches once the index reports the question settled; and an item whose index call fails holds with `questions-unknown` rather than dispatching. Today's parser reads dash bullets only, so six queued items whose documents number their questions report zero — the case this replaces.

items.title: The planner reads open questions from Vantage's index, and an item waiting on one holds as `question-open`

criteria.text: The questions the board and the planner act on come from Vantage's own index (`vantage-check index --format json`, whose `questions[]` carries `id`, `state`, `preference`, `title`, `leaning`, `blockedOn`), not from the dash-bullet parser in `tools/tillr-view/questions.go`. Measured today: that parser reports zero questions for the six documents that number theirs.

The three answers stay distinct and are tested: the tool's list; `questions-unknown` when the tool is absent, fails, or times out; `design-doc-missing` when the item names a file that is not there. Unknown must never read as no questions.

`tillr drain plan` holds such an item with reason `question-open` instead of dispatching it, and the item's projected state says so, so the rail and the header can count it — proven by planting a question in a fixture document and watching the item stop being dispatchable.

The Vantage-index plumbing this builds is one reader, not two: `item-drain-question-hold` (`1`) is the item that stops a drain on an open question, and this item reuses its index reader rather than writing a second parser beside it. Its `blocked_by` names that item so the order is the queue's, not a comment's.

items.title: A lane root scopes its branch name, so a stale lane elsewhere cannot block every future drain

criteria.text: Two lane roots of one repository can each stage `lane-1` in the same drain: the branch a lane commits onto is scoped by its lane root (or the stager refuses by naming the other root) instead of `func laneBranch(lane string) string { return "tillr/" + lane }` at `tools/tillr-drain/drain/stage.go:296`, which the acceptance run measured as `fatal: cannot force update the branch 'tillr/lane-1' used by worktree at …/canary/lanes/lane-1/worktree`.

A test stages lane 1 in two lane roots of one repository and asserts both succeed, and that a stale registration whose directory still exists is named in the refusal rather than left to git's `fatal:` line — `clearWorktree` prunes only registrations whose directories are gone, so today the second root fails.

items.title: A run records which of the policy's model routes served it

criteria.text: A terminal run record names the route its dispatch drew: `tillr run status <run-id> --json` carries the model id staging put into the adapter's argv, and the `runs` row carries the same value. Today neither does: `tools/tillr-run/run/apply.go`'s `Record` and the `runs` DDL in `tools/tillr-run/run/schema.go` name `backend` and no model id, so no reader can say which of `config/tillr/backend-policy.json`'s seven `pi.models` routes answered a run, which is the attribution day-2's failure criterion 7 calls lost eval attribution.

The recorded route is the one the adapter was handed and not a second draw: a test runs a request whose `Command` carries a model id and asserts that the record and the row name that argv element, so a record naming a route the adapter never received fails the test. Today `rg -n 'route' tools/tillr-run/run/apply.go tools/tillr-run/run/schema.go` returns nothing, so such a test cannot exist yet.

items.title: The floor's routing order lives once in model_facts and the seven per-row blocks are gone

criteria.text: `rg -c 'openrouter_routing' tag-personal/config/yolo-jail/config.d/personal.toml` answers 1 or 2 (the `model_facts` block plus its comment) and every `[providers.openrouter.models.*.openrouter_routing]` block is deleted; today it answers 9, at lines 29, 122, 132, 167, 177, 187, 204 and 214.

Every OpenRouter row inherits one routing order, and `tests/yolo-config.test.sh` asserts the inherited shape so a row that grows its own block again fails a test instead of waiting to be spotted in a diff.

items.title: The observatory's snapshot says why the loop stopped, from the loop's own result file

criteria.text: `last_stop_reason` is assigned from the loop's `<root>/.tillr/loop/drain-<stamp>.json` result: today `rg -n 'LastStopReason' tools/` returns exactly one line, the field's own declaration at `tools/tillr-view/serve.go:344`, so the snapshot renders `null` for every stop and a reader cannot tell `queue-drained` from a fault.

The snapshot no longer tells the reader the reason is owed by another slice: `rg -n 'which OBS-1 adds' tools/tillr-view/` returns the hardcoded `StopNote` text today (in `serve.go` and in a web fixture), and after the change a test pins that a result file naming `queue-drained` renders as `last_stop_reason: "queue-drained"` rather than as a note about what is missing.

items.title: A held lane is never reported as a drained queue, and stopping the loop stops its run — two lies the first night's drain told

criteria.text: `drain loop` never reports `queue-drained` while any item holds `no-lane`: `ReasonNoLane` is only reachable after the blocker, state, retry, policy and capacity rules have already passed, so it proves dispatchable work exists right now. Measured 2026-11-14: take 4 stopped after 0 ticks with `queue-drained — a full tick planned nothing dispatchable: 60 held item(s)` while all 60 held `no-lane`, because `lane-1` was still leased to a run the operator had killed; `docs/design/tillr-day2.md` §4.3 already requires 0 ready AND 0 active leases before that word is used.

A lane held by a finite lease is waited on, not turned into a stop: the loop waits interruptibly until the earliest `leased_until` and re-plans, per `docs/design/momentum-principle.md`'s “drained is idle, not exited”. A lane held with no expiry is a hard non-zero stop named `lanes-leased`, which tells the operator `tillr run release` is the missing act — the two cases are different facts and the stop reason says which one happened.

Stopping the loop stops the run: `tillr drain loop` and `tillr run exec` install `signal.NotifyContext` for SIGINT and SIGTERM instead of `context.Background()`, so a stop cancels the run context, `cmd.Cancel` kills the process group, the terminal `runs` row and the lane's `freeLane` are written, and the stop is recorded as an operator stop. Measured 2026-11-14: `pkill -f 'tillr drain loop'` left an orphaned `pi` worker that finished a minute later and committed `110669bce2` onto `tillr/lane-1` — a candidate nobody judged — while its lane stayed leased for another 32 minutes.

A test pins both halves against a fixture loop: a tick whose every hold is `no-lane` over a finite lease waits and re-plans rather than stopping, a tick with no dispatch and a NULL lease stops `lanes-leased` non-zero, and a SIGTERM to a loop with a live run leaves no `tillr-run exec` process behind and writes exactly one terminal `runs` row.

items.title: A harness-failed item can be re-dispatched by an authorized retry link — today `run-link-missing` is a parking space, not a queue

criteria.text: An item whose only failure was the harness — a fence the brief made mandatory, a stale binary, an operator stop — can be re-dispatched, and the decision names the run it supersedes. `mayBeARetry` (`tools/tillr-drain/drain/plan.go`) holds any item with a terminal `runs` row as `run-link-missing` forever, so today a failed item is a parking space: measured 2026-11-14, seven items are held that way and none can move without an operator hand-editing the store.

The retry is authorized and recorded, not silent: it carries who asked, why, and which run it supersedes, and the record survives in the store so the second attempt is attributable. A retry that overwrites the first run's record is the defect, not the feature.

The distinction the trap needs is a claim, not a guess: `tillr drain plan` can tell a candidate the harness refused (no judgment was ever made) from a candidate the gate judged and failed, and only the first is retryable by link. Measured 2026-11-14: three refusals in take 5 were `boundary-scope-escape` before the gate ran, yet each consumed its item.

items.title: The drain says which build it is running, so a fix is never called closed from a tree the process never loaded

criteria.text: `tillr drain loop` stamps its own source revision and digest into its startup output and into every `drain-*.json` it writes, the way `tillr-view`'s `build.go` already does: `producer.version` is a hardcoded `"0.1.0"` today, so two different builds are indistinguishable in the record. Measured 2026-11-14: a fence fix (`979501265d`) was committed, gated and pack-mirrored while the loop ran `~/.yolo/bin/launch/tillr-drain`, built at 00:37 that morning, and three items were refused by the very trap the fix closed.

An in-launch drain can be pointed at a build that carries the work, and the handoff is explicit: a documented source root or durable bin directory, prepended to `PATH` for the loop and its children, with the eight binaries built together because `ProcessSteps` resolves `tillr-{drain,run,item,gate,land}` through `PATH`. `docs/design/tillr-distribution.md` §9 and `.justfile` currently claim a mechanism the tree does not have, and the claim is corrected or made true.

A test pins the honest half: a build stamp appears in the loop's first line of output and in the record it writes, and a record without one is drawn as a build that cannot be named rather than trusted — the same distinction `tillr-view`'s `--ui-at` and stale-server note already make.

items.title: Execution state is derived from runs and verdicts while the stored state keeps only what the owner decided, so no item can be parked `in-progress` by a failure nobody judged

criteria.text: `items.state` stores owner disposition only — `not-started`, `in-queue`, `blocked`, `landed`, `resolved-elsewhere`, `closed` — and "Being worked on" and "In the merge queue" are derived from live leases and unretired attempts. Measured 2026-11-14: no derivation can tell `blocked` (an owner hold) or `closed` (won't-do) from `in-queue` (admitted to work), which is why the stored value has to keep the owner's half and give up the harness's. `checkState` (`tools/tillr-item/item/apply.go:201`) is a membership test on seven strings with no `from -> to` table, so today `SetState` writes any writable state over any other and `in-progress` is a one-way door with no review queue.

Derived dispatchability sits BESIDE `mayBeARetry` rather than subsuming it. If "no live run and no unretired judged verdict" replaced `mayBeARetry`, then every 30-minute timeout (`AttemptUnjudged`, zero `gate.verdict`), every `boundary-scope-escape` (`fenceViolation` runs before `Gate`, zero `gate.verdict`) and every `candidate-no-op` (`head == base`, zero `gate.verdict`) would re-dispatch immediately and burn money in a loop. A test pins each of those three shapes as HELD with its own reason, never `ReasonNotReady`.

`failCandidate` stops writing `StateInProgress`, and `Loop.settle` never calls `Steps.Verdict(..., VerdictFailed)` for a candidate `Gate` did not judge. Measured 2026-11-14: `failCandidate` (`tools/tillr-drain/drain/loop.go:1179`) calls `Verdict(ctx, candidate, VerdictFailed)` at `:1180` and then `ItemState(..., StateInProgress)`, so a `RESULT: blocked` report — a spec conflict, not a failing candidate — freezes every criterion `not-done` through `carryCriteria` (`tools/tillr-item/item/apply.go:241`) and leaves a human no way to edit them. A `RESULT: blocked` outcome moves the item to `blocked` with its criteria untouched.

`ProjectItemState` never emits `"working"` when `active == nil`. Measured 2026-11-14: its own comment (`tools/tillr-view/serveread.go:645`) says "`in-progress` reads as Working only while a run is live", while the `switch` at `:665` sets `p.State = "working"` for `case "in-progress"` unconditionally — which is how the board displayed "8 working" over zero live lanes. The projection and the planner agree, asserted by the case below.

One cross-module round-trip test (`TestEveryNonLandingOutcomeRecoversAndAgreesWithView`, in `drain` and `view`) drives four fixture items through `fenceViolation`, `RESULT: blocked`, `GateFailed` and `StateTimedOut`, and asserts: (i) zero items hold with `ReasonNotReady`; (ii) each class re-dispatches through its documented verb without manual `tillr item state` surgery; (iii) `ProjectItemState` never emits `"working"` when `active == nil`; and (iv) `boardCountsOf(...).Dispatchable` (`tools/tillr-view/counts.go:35`, which today ignores `mayBeARetry` and overcounts by 6) equals the exact count `drain.Plan` dispatches given infinite lanes.

items.title: A tick's record and events carry the correlation id the trace key needs, so a run is recovered by key rather than by string search

criteria.text: The `run.request` a tick emits carries `correlation_id` naming the tick and the item, and the events the tick appends carry the same value: today `rg -n 'CorrelationID' tools/tillr-drain/` returns nothing — `requestEnvelope` in `drain/once.go` sets none — while the record envelope declares the field at `tools/tillr/record/envelope.go:35`, so the `trace_key` `session-recording.md` specifies can only be a string search through payloads.

A test drives one tick against a scratch store and reads the run's `run.allocate` row and its request back by correlation id alone, so a tick that stops stamping it fails the suite instead of leaving the timeline's first hop unjoinable.

items.title: A refused or isolated landing attempt is an event, so a reader can see why an item is still in the queue

criteria.text: A landing attempt that answers `refused` or `isolated` appends a store event naming the candidate, the result and the reason, so `tillr view events` answers why the item is still queued: today `land.attempt` is a stdout record kind and never an event — `tools/tillr-land/land/schema.go:113` says so in its own comment — and `rg -n 'AttemptKind' tools/tillr-land/land/*.go` finds the declaration and no `AppendEvent`.

A test lands a candidate whose trunk moved and asserts the attempt's refusal is readable from the store's event table, not only from the face's stdout, so the fact `land.land` alone cannot express survives the process that saw it.

items.title: A drain that dies before its first tick leaves a terminal record, not four lines on a stderr nobody kept

criteria.text: A `tillr drain loop` that cannot start — a policy that does not load, a root with no store — writes `<root>/.tillr/loop/drain-<stamp>.json` naming the fault and its exit code, so the failure is readable after the terminal is gone: today the result file is written only by a running loop — `rg -n 'recordResult|LoopResultFile' tools/tillr-drain/main.go` answers nothing, and `fail` prints to stderr — which is board item 612's class re-measured against the successor and still open.
A test runs the loop face with an unreadable policy and asserts the terminal record exists and names the refusal, so a startup death cannot go silent again.

items.title: A tick indexes what it observed, so Layer B is filled without a human running the indexer

criteria.text: The loop invokes the trace indexer at the end of a tick: today `rg -n 'tillr-trace|tillr_trace' tools/tillr-drain/` returns nothing, which is why the acceptance run's `index.db` held no `runs_index` row for either run and every Layer B row rendered `unobserved_seam` until a human ran the indexer by hand.

A test drives one tick against a scratch store and asserts the run appears in the trace index afterwards, so a tick that stops indexing fails the suite instead of turning the timeline into a gap that renders correctly and truthfully says nothing.

items.title: The loop's one-hop failover is exercised end to end, not just wired

criteria.text: An infrastructure failure walks exactly one hop: driven through `tillr drain loop` with a policy naming `pi` then `agy` and a first adapter that exits 4, the store holds two `run.record`s for the item, the second naming backend `agy`, and the item is not held as `run-infra-exhausted`. Today nothing exercises that path: `rg -n 'agy|-f1' tools/tillr-drain/loop_test.go` returns nothing, and the only failover coverage is `tools/tillr-drain/drain/policy_test.go`'s hop arithmetic.

The lane is reset before the retry, so the second attempt's candidate carries nothing the first attempt left in the worktree: the failover run's base sha equals the trunk the tick started from, and the test asserts it rather than assuming it.

items.title: A patch-series item is queueable: a fence that names its checkout, and a lane that may move a patch ref

criteria.text: A fork-series item can be staged and dispatched: `allowed_paths` can name the checkout under `.forks/lanes/<lane>/<fork>`, the boundary bracket excuses `refs/heads/patch/<fork>` for that lane, and `tillr-land` advances or refuses that ref alongside `main` — today `rg -n 'forks/lanes|refs/heads/patch' tools/tillr-drain tools/tillr-land -g '*.go'` returns one comment and no code, and `rg -n 'patch/|forks/lanes' tools/tillr-drain -g '*_test.go'` matches a comment in `seed_test.go` that says the opposite: a lane worktree cut from `main` cannot succeed on a `patch/pi` item.

A test drives one fork-series item through stage, boundary and land against a scratch repository that carries a `patch/<name>` branch, and asserts the patch ref moved exactly once and the trunk moved only through `land pass` — because today the movement trips `host-boundary-violation` and halts the loop.

items.title: The observatory's two-item acceptance walkthrough is reproduced and recorded

criteria.text: Section 6's acceptance walkthrough is reproduced against a live store and recorded in the document: two queued items are drained through `tillr drain loop`, `just observatory` serves the result, both items project as `Landed`, and the walkthrough's questions are answered one at a time with what was actually seen — each of the seven stages, every Layer A record exchange, and each run's token and USD cost. Today the section states the experiment and no dated record of one exists.

Every answer carries the epistemic badge Section 2.3 requires rather than a green: a stage or claim whose evidence is absent is written down as a gap with the badge that says why it is missing (`unobserved_seam`, `derived_clock`, `unreadable`), so a reader can tell what was observed from what was inferred.

items.title: The per-seat bounds the encoding already carries are handed to a launch, not left as data

criteria.text: The budgets the encoding already carries reach a launch: `yolo-packs/seat-profiles/files/seat-profiles.json` states `bounds.<seat>.budgets.toolCalls`, `.tokens` and `.wallMs` for each seat (scout is `30 / 150000 / 600000`), and today `rg -n 'toolBudget|usageBudget|wallMs' yolo-packs/matt/pack.json` returns nothing, so no seat's stated bound is rendered into the composed subagents config that would enforce it.

A test pins one seat's stated bound through to the composed subagents config, so a seat whose bound silently stops being rendered fails the suite rather than being noticed when a runaway child spends past its cap.

items.title: The designer seat is pinned to a row, so an unnamed dispatch cannot silently fall to the floor

criteria.text: `designer.md`'s frontmatter names its `model:` row: today `rg -n '^model:' yolo-packs/matt/files/pi/agent/agents/designer.md` returns nothing, so a dispatch that names no model reaches whatever the floor resolves to and returns a plausible document with nothing on its face saying which row wrote it.

A designer run on the degraded row is stamped as degraded: today `rg -n 'seat-degraded' yolo-packs/` returns nothing anywhere, so the stamp the ruling requires exists in no pack and a floor-produced document is indistinguishable from one the pinned seat produced.

items.title: A decision records an automated reviewer as its decider instead of attributing it to the whale

criteria.text: A decision's `decided_by` accepts an `autoqa` value, so a harness's decision does not attribute itself to the whale: today the store refuses it by construction — `tools/tillr-item/item/schema.go:105` is `decided_by TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decided_by IN ('owner','whale'))` — while the verdict schema beside it already carries `ActorAutoQA` (`item/verdict.go:37`).
A conformance case records a decision with `decided_by: autoqa` and reads it back, and a case still refuses a value outside the closed set, so the new member cannot be spelled by accident.

items.title: The landing tier runs in shadow beside the gate and records what it would have done

criteria.text: A candidate can be run through the landing tier without anything landing, and the run writes a record naming each check's tier and the wall clock its tier would have cost: today `rg -n 'shadow' tools/tillr-gate/ tools/tillr-land/` returns nothing, so the `tier` field `tools/tillr-gate/registry.go:99` declares is planned and never compared against a real gate's answer.

A test pins that a shadow run of one candidate writes its record and moves no ref, and that two shadow records over the same candidate diff mechanically, so the flip that §10 sequences second is decided from a measurement rather than from the estimate the document itself flags as one.

items.title: The landing document names the one lander the tree now has

criteria.text: The landing document names one lander: `rg -n 'tools/mq|bin/land' docs/design/landing-principles.md` returns nothing, and every *Scope* and *Enforced by* line that binds a lander names `tools/tillr-land`. Today it returns 6 lines naming `tools/mq` and 3 naming `bin/land` while `ls tools/mq bin/land` fails for both, so those lines send a reader to programs the tree no longer has.

A reader asking which program lands a pipeline candidate reaches no page presenting a retired one as live: `docs/design/land-3i-inventory.md`'s frontmatter and its recommendation say which lander was kept and where the ruling is recorded rather than offering the choice as open, and the commit names every design document it leaves citing `tools/mq` for a reason, so `rg -ln 'tools/mq' docs/design/` is a judged list rather than a roll of dead links.

`docs/design/land-3i-inventory.md` stops carrying dead links: the 36 link targets that name `tools/mq`, `bin/land` or `yolo-packs/merge-queue` become backticked paths, so the document renders as a record of programs the tree no longer has rather than as 36 broken links. The inventory is a historical record and is not rewritten; only the link syntax changes, and the commit message says so.

items.title: The settle bell coalesces its rings and honours an alerts.bell.settle setting that turns it off

criteria.text: `turn-bell.ts` coalesces settle rings inside a short per-session window and reads an `alerts.bell.settle` setting that can disable the bell entirely: today `rg -n 'coalesc|cooldown|alerts' yolo-packs/matt/files/extensions/turn-bell.ts` returns nothing, so neither the cooldown nor the setting named in the item's own criterion exists.

Tests prove both halves separately: a bell that rings twice inside the window fails one case, and a bell that still rings with `alerts.bell.settle` off fails the other, so the off switch cannot be dropped while the cooldown still passes.

items.title: One supported profiler command, and the second tool retired or delegating

criteria.text: Exactly one command profiles a live pi given only --pid and --seconds, and the other tool either delegates to it or is removed: `ls tools/pi-profile-live.mjs` fails or the file documents its delegation, and one tracked doc names the supported command.

The kept output carries a machine-readable summary naming the sample count and self% plus inclusive% for at least the top 15 functions, so two runs diff mechanically; and tests cover the refusal cases -- no listener, several listeners, a non-node pid.

items.title: Each tillr binary carries a README with its Known Gaps banner, and the gate checks documented faces against live --help

criteria.text: Every one of the eight binary modules carries a `README.md` that opens with the stamped Known Gaps callout: today only two modules have one — `ls tools/tillr*/README.md` answers `tools/tillr-loop/README.md` and `tools/tillr-trace/README.md`, and `ls tools/tillr-cli/README.md tools/tillr-drain/README.md` fails for both, so the pack ships source with no standalone judgment beside it.

A repository test extracts every `tillr[-<noun>] <noun> <face>` invocation from the module READMEs and the `tillr-operating` skill, runs the documented face's `--help`, and fails on a face that does not exist or on a Markdown flag table — today the only `--help` assertion in the tree is `tools/tillr-cli/main_test.go`'s own dispatcher case, and `rg -ln -- '--help' tests/` names no tillr conformance test.

items.title: agent-runtime.md's backend boundary names the process-and-records form tillr accepted

criteria.text: `docs/design/agent-runtime.md` section 3 states the boundary tillr built — an adapter program behind a `run.request`'s argv and a record, no Go interface — and says which section of `tillr-muse-backend.md` supersedes its in-process sketch: today the sketch stands unamended at section 3, where "The two kinds share exactly one interface ... the agent-specific members live in a sub-interface" is still the ruling, and `tillr-muse-backend.md` section 8 says the amendment is "owed by that document's owner".

A reader following the boundary from either document reaches the same construction: the amended section names `run.request`'s `Command` and the `backend` field as the seam and links the ruling, so `rg -n 'process and a request record|argv seam' docs/design/agent-runtime.md` answers the new sentence rather than nothing.

items.title: A determination: where the provider-allowlist source lives

criteria.text: Owner decision recorded in docs/design/design-seat-replacement-ruling.md and this item's state leaves `blocked`: a research deliverable with no artifact it must produce, so no criterion can name one; its build half is item-designer-pin.

items.title: `tillr view status` answers the board's counts, so the header's numbers have a command behind them

criteria.text: `tillr view status --store <path>` answers a `counts` object with `by_state`, `dispatchable`, `blocked` and `runs_live`, computed from the same rows the snapshot uses, so the four figures are identical to the wire's on the same store.
A test pins the CLI's counts against a fixture store whose expected numbers are written by hand, and a second case shows the CLI and the served snapshot answering the same figures for the same store.
The board's header reads the number a `tillr` command prints for the same store: measured by running both against `/workspace/.tillr/state.db` and diffing the four values.

items.title: A shared refusal component renders an unknown code as a refusal naming the code, on every pane

criteria.text: One component renders every refusal the face can produce, and an unrecognised `error.code` renders as *the face refused: `<code>`* with the server's message, never as an empty panel.
The rail, the item pane and the evidence pane each use it, and a test drives an unknown code through all three and asserts the code is visible in each.

The document pane's four codes (`no-design-doc`, `design-doc-missing`, `design-doc-outside-root`, `design-doc-unreadable`) keep their own sentences through the same component rather than a parallel `switch`.

items.title: State is encoded three ways on every surface, including a glyph that survives greyscale

criteria.text: A glyph accompanies the colour and the word for all seven projected states, distinct per state, rendered by one component rather than by each surface.
A capture-time check proves it: the board rendered in greyscale still distinguishes a blocked row from an in-queue one, and the glyphs are compared against a written table rather than eyeballed.

items.title: A running item appears in a now band, with its elapsed time labelled as the viewer's clock

criteria.text: A band pinned above the rail shows every live run: item title, lane, elapsed, and the lease left, drawn from `lanes` and `runs` without moving the item's row in the order.
A live elapsed is labelled as the viewer's clock and a recorded duration as the recorded pair; no surface presents the first as the second.
With no run live the band is absent rather than an empty box, which is the same rule the truthfulness table states for every other absence.

items.title: A pause control stops every automatic update, and a selected item never changes under the reader

criteria.text: A header control stops both update paths — the live channel's invalidations and the polling timer — and says so while it is on, with the age of what is being read; resuming re-reads once.

With a pause on, a write to the store changes nothing on screen; with it off, a write that touches the selected item updates the rail and the counts but never replaces the selected item or moves the pane.
A test drives selection then a store write and asserts the selection and the pane's subject are unchanged, which is the assertion that fails today's board.

Every open-question code span the change relies on is a link, not a bare code span. The predecessor failed the gate in 7.8 s on `90:9 error ref/unlinked-oq` for a bare `OQ-OBD1` in `tools/tillr-view/web/README.md` — a real candidate defect inside its own fence, not a fence trap — so this criterion names the fix and the checker that proves it: `uvx vantage-check` passes on both the source README and its `pack-sync` mirror, and the question is linked as `<vantage base>/#/<path>#OQ-OBD1` the way the rest of the corpus spells it.

items.title: The item pane shows a document's metadata and a Vantage link, and stops rendering the document

criteria.text: `GET /api/v1/items/{id}/doc` answers `frontmatter`, `path`, `anchor` and `open_questions`, and no `markdown`; the four refusal codes keep their own sentences.
The pane renders the frontmatter card, the question count, the path, and a link built as `<base>/#/<path>` (plus the section anchor when the item names one) from a user-scope base URL.
With no base URL configured the link is drawn and inert and the pane says so in one line; the board never probes the URL.
The `vantage-md` rendering, the question index and the disagreement display are removed from the board, and the dependency goes with them.

items.title: One command answers what is running right now, joining live lanes with finished runs and the loop's own stop record

criteria.text: `tillr view running --store <path> [--watch] [--json]` exists in `tools/tillr-view/` and prints three blocks: a loop-and-lane header (`lanes leased: M/K`, the loop's last stop reason), the active runs (`lane_id`, `item_id`, `rank`, `title`, elapsed, lease left, the run's `.log` path, or an explicit `0 live runs; lanes idle: lane-1`), and the last five finished runs with their outcome (`landed <sha>`, `gate-failed`, `exited <code>`, `timed-out`), duration and cost. `--watch` re-renders once a second in a terminal and `--json` emits the record envelope instead of the table.

The header refuses to present a stale stop record as current: when `event_head_seq` postdates the newest `.tillr/loop/drain-*.json`, it says so — `"stale stop record — newer run exists at seq <N>"` — because that is exactly the shape that hid take 6's 15:21Z death, where the newest loop file was take 5's and nothing on the board said the loop had stopped.

The view joins three sources and says why no two of them suffice: `liveRuns` (lanes, runs, allocations; `tools/tillr-view/serve.go:594`) because `run.Exec` writes no `runs` row until `writeTerminal` runs and `run/apply.go:125` clears `lanes.run_id` on release, plus recent terminal `runs` rows, plus `.tillr/loop/drain-*.json`. A test builds a store with one live lane, one finished run and one loop file and asserts each appears in the block it belongs to and nowhere else.

The webapp header carries an always-visible lane pill (`0/1 lanes running · idle` or `2/2 lanes running`) beside the R37 `ProjectItemState` fix, while the `NowBand` stays absent when `RunsLive == 0` — so a stopped board says the lanes are idle rather than wearing a `working` glyph over nothing, and it does not merely replace one invisible state with a band that appears only when there is work.

items.title: Retire the retired work board's documents, keeping what tillr still cites

criteria.text: Every document whose subject is the retired work board is inventoried by path and classified as live-for-tillr, superseded, or already archived, and the classification is written down before anything is deleted.

Each retired document is absorbed first and archived second: every fact tillr still relies on (the item state model, the utilities contract, the failure diagnosis) exists in a surviving document, and the retirement record says which document took it.
No tracked document calls the observatory's queue screen `the board` without saying so, and no surviving document describes the retired tool as present-tense machinery.
The stale `board` binary on PATH is named as a host-side leftover to remove, not something this repository ships: nothing in the tree builds or declares it.

items.title: A tillr item asks for a seat, and the policy maps the seat to a model, so swapping a model never touches an item

criteria.text: An item names a SEAT (design, build, review, scout) and never a model id; the policy maps each seat to a backend and a model, so `pi-designer` is reached by asking for the design seat rather than by listing an item id in `overrides`. Measured today: `overrides` is item-id keyed and empty, so nothing reaches the Carbon backend that the policy already declares.

Swapping which model designs — or moving the design seat to another backend — is a one-line policy change that touches no item, proven by swapping one in a fixture store and dispatching the same item to the other model.

A seat the policy does not map, or an item naming a seat that does not exist, is refused at plan time with the seat and the mapped seats in the message — never silently defaulted to the tick's backend.
The request a seat dispatch stages records which seat it was and which backend answered, so a run's provenance explains the model it used without reading the policy that was live at the time.

items.title: The pi fork's UI latency campaign: every measured stall has a named cause, a fix, and a test that fails without it

criteria.text: A measured inventory replaces the anecdote: each UI path (keystroke to render, tool call to first paint, streaming token to paint, resize, the fleet panel's per-second clock redraw, the editor's own per-keystroke work) has a p50/p95 number on this machine, captured with the method that produced it, and the ones already fixed are marked inside this note rather than assumed fixed (the handoff's own warning: 'do not mistake existing fixes for complete fixes').
Each remaining stall has a named cause with its file and function in the fork, and a fix that lands as a patch in the series — not as a local edit — with the measurement repeated after it.
A regression test per fixed stall that fails when the fix is reverted, and a standing budget the suite asserts, so the next change that puts a stall back fails the gate rather than a session.

The document ends up saying what was measured, what was fixed, and what was deliberately left with the reason — including the usage-caching decision this campaign inherits, so a reader knows whether the footer still costs a frame.

items.title: A killed run resumes its own session instead of starting cold — today the lane's session-id file is never written, so a 17M-token attempt is unrecoverable and its cache is paid for twice

criteria.text: The stager mints a session id and writes it to `<lane-dir>/session-id`, which `run-pi` already reads and passes as `--session-id`. Measured 2026-11-14: nothing in the repository writes that file — its only writer is `tests/tillr-muse-backend.test.py` — so the file is empty, `pi` mints its own id, and the driver never learns which session a run used. The evidence is a killed run's 234 KB session sitting under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--workspace-.tillr-lanes-lane-1-worktree--/` that the loop cannot name.

A run that died without a verdict can be resumed from its own session, reusing the lane, the brief and the fence, and the resume reuses the provider's prefix cache rather than paying for the whole transcript again. A resume must be one attempt continued and not a second attempt: the run id stays, the retry budget is untouched, and the store records the resume as a new span on the same run rather than a new `runs` row.

A resume re-takes the boundary snapshot and re-derives the fence before continuing, because a run killed after its worker committed would otherwise be judged against a bracket taken at dispatch. A test drives a run killed after a commit and asserts the resumed run's boundary bracket is the one re-taken at resume, not the one staged before it — the negative control is that the stale bracket admits a change the fence refuses.

items.title: The owner rules whether an automated sign-off reader is built, now that the Pi judge it was reduced from is deleted

criteria.text: Owner decision recorded in docs/design/work-control-judge-in-tillr.md and this item's state leaves `blocked`: the mechanical path retires what the pipeline lands, and every completion with no landing behind it — a foreground session's commits, a criterion about a document's contents, the `defective` finding — stands claimed and unretired with no reader, because the extension that judged it (`work-control.ts`) is no longer in the pack and no approver job was ever built.

items.title: The owner rules how a blocked item resumes, now that the turn-end trigger that watched its condition is deleted

criteria.text: Owner decision recorded in docs/design/tillr-day2.md and this item's state leaves `blocked`: the planner's `blocked` hold reads `blocked_by` edges only and the item record has no field for a resume condition, so a park that named an external event (`head-move`, a run completion, a timeout) resumes only when a person moves the item — the design sentence `work-control-judge-in-tillr.md` says the drain document must say has not been written, and whether one is wanted is the owner's.

items.title: The pi series' behavioral tail moves into settings and extensions

criteria.text: Each of the five behaviors the series still carries as a patch -- the cache-warming horizon, tool bounds, the Bedrock provider request, the session list and misc UX -- is carried by a setting or an extension on the published patch branch rather than by a patch, and the change names where each removed behavior now lives.
A stranger can name every removed patch and its replacement by reading the commit that removes it, and the fork-quality suite passes at the branch tip.

items.title: visibleWidth measures a settled string once, behind a bounded memo

criteria.text: The width memo in packages/tui/src/utils.ts exposes a stats accessor and a reset accessor shaped like getTruncateCacheStats/resetTruncateCache, and a pure-ASCII string reaches the memo instead of being re-scanned by asciiVisibleWidth on every call.

The memo is bounded by entries and by characters with a per-entry key cap, and a bench over stated corpora (pure ASCII, ANSI-styled ASCII, non-ASCII; short and long) shows repeat measurement of a long settled string at least 3x faster than its first measurement and no more than 10% slower for short or never-repeated strings, with the before/after numbers on one machine in the commit.
The tui test suite passes unchanged and visibleWidth returns the same width for every string in it.

items.title: A thinking stream that repeats itself is aborted and named

criteria.text: A model thinking stream that repeats a sentence or two is aborted with a recorded reason before it reaches 30k tokens, and a test feeding a synthetic repeating stream asserts the abort fires.
A turn whose thinking stream is aborted still completes: the truncated thinking is kept with its recorded reason and the assistant turn does not fail.

items.title: `*-pi-automode.jsonl` sidecars carry no `responseId` or `tokStats`, so session scanners ingest unattributed stripped duplicates

criteria.text: Measured: every `*-pi-automode.jsonl` assistant record carries only `role`, `model` and `usage` — no `responseId` (`gen-...`) and no `tokStats` — while a regular session stamps both. Record the counts for one session of each kind before changing anything, so the claim is observed rather than asserted.

The fix is one of the two named routes and says which: stamp `responseId` and `tokStats` onto the automode sidecar's assistant messages, or move `*-pi-automode.jsonl` out of `agent/sessions/` so a session scanner cannot ingest it. A third route is acceptable only if it states why neither of these works.

A scanner reading the sessions directory either attributes every assistant record it ingests to a `responseId`, or skips the sidecar by name. Demonstrated on a real directory: the count of unattributed records is zero, and the count of regular-session records is unchanged.
